script: They demanded my credit card physically—my peace was destroyed.. I checked into the hotel, and the front desk clerk asked for my credit card. I said, "Just use the one on file." She stared, then said, "I still need to see the physical card." I laughed, "Seriously? I've never been asked for one before." She shrugged, "It's just policy—verify it's actually your card, not someone else's." The same thing happened with my corporate stay. They said, "We need your card or an authorization form from the company." I pointed out, "The company card is on file. It's already paid through a third‑party." She replied, "We don't have your payment details because you didn't pay us. We still need to see the card." I said, "I didn't bring it. Of course I didn't." She said, "We need the physical card." Then I tried tapping my phone. "Sorry, we don't accept tap‑to‑pay for check‑in—only for room service and mini‑bar." She repeated, "Just use the card in the reservation. We need the physical card." I was like, "I didn't bring it. Of course I didn't." Every time, the clerk kept insisting on the physical card, even though the reservation already had a valid card on file. Why do they think they can just use any card listed without knowing who it belongs to? They've never had to ask for a card before, and now they're getting mad reviews for being a "hassle" at check‑in. I am like, "Honestly, if you can't handle a simple policy, you're not ready for the real world."
